rights: Original fictional paper-only games. No real scientific, historical or mechanical claim is required.

games.title: The Coral Chart Expedition
games.opening: The research ship has five loose pages from a fictional survey. Work as a crew to rebuild the route and send the captain one checked report.
games.ending: The captain thanks your crew. The repaired chart can guide the next pretend paper expedition.

stages.title: Find the survey station
stages.setup: The log says: choose the station with a BLUE flag and exactly THREE wave marks. Colour words and counts are both printed; do not rely on colour alone.
cards: Reef A | blue flag | two waves
Reef B | blue flag | three waves
Reef C | red flag | three waves
stages.prompt: Which station should the crew inspect?
stages.why: Only Reef B has both the blue flag and three waves.
hints: Read both conditions in the log.
A station with only one matching condition is not enough.
Reef B has blue and three waves.
stages.skip: Give the crew BLUE-3 and move to the chart.

stages.title: Locate the chart square
stages.setup: Find your station code in this chart key: BLUE-2 = A1; BLUE-3 = C2; RED-3 = D4. Use the code from the log, not a guess from the drawing.
stages.prompt: Which square matches the log code?
stages.why: The key maps BLUE-3 to C2.
hints: Keep the complete code from checkpoint 1.
Read the middle row of the key.
BLUE-3 points to C2.
stages.skip: Give the crew C2 and continue with the observation cards.

stages.title: Compare the three observations
stages.setup: At C2, the Navigator says the route must touch a buoy. The Observer says it must avoid the red marker. The Recorder says it must pass east of the square.
cards: North Passage | buoy | red marker | west
East Passage | buoy | no red marker | east
South Passage | no buoy | no red marker | east
stages.prompt: Which passage satisfies all three crew notes?
stages.why: Only East Passage has a buoy, no red marker and an eastward position.
hints: Share all three role notes.
Cross out any passage with a red marker or no buoy.
East Passage satisfies all conditions.
stages.skip: Give the crew EAST; keep the role evidence for the final report.

stages.title: Order the record strips
stages.setup: The EAST passage record says the Kelp note came first, the Reef note came after Kelp, and the Channel note came last.
stages.prompt: What is the correct record order?
stages.why: Kelp first, Reef next and Channel last makes K-R-C.
hints: Place the first and last strips before the middle.
K is first and C is last.
The remaining R sits between them.
stages.skip: Give the crew K-R-C for the report.

stages.title: Send the captain's report
stages.setup: A valid report must include the station code, chart square, passage and record order that your crew earned. Compare your written results with the three candidate reports.
stages.prompt: Which report is fully supported by your paper evidence?
stages.why: Report 1 is the only report consistent with all four earlier results.
hints: Read the results in checkpoint order.
Check the square and passage before the final order.
All four results match Report 1.
stages.skip: Use Report 1 and read the ending.

games.title: The Mixed-Up Exhibition
games.opening: A fictional museum opens tomorrow, but one exhibit label has wandered away. Your curators must compare marks, case notes and a floor plan to put it back.
roles: Map keeper follows the gallery route
games.ending: The exhibit is ready. Visitors can read its correct fictional story because your curators checked every clue.

stages.title: Read the lost ticket
stages.setup: The ticket shows TWO crescent marks and ONE star. The gallery ledger says: Amber has two crescents and one star; Blue has one crescent and two stars; Green has two crescents and no star.
stages.prompt: Where does the ticket belong?
stages.why: Amber alone matches both crescent count and star count.
hints: Count both kinds of mark.
Two crescents are not enough without the star.
Amber matches all three marks.

stages.title: Walk the gallery route
stages.setup: The Amber floor plan says: start at the door, go past Case 2, then turn right to the case beside the window. The window-side cases are Case 4 and Case 7; only Case 4 is to the right of Case 2.
cards: Case 4 | right of Case 2, by window
stages.prompt: Which case is on the ticket route?
stages.why: Case 4 is both right of Case 2 and beside the window.
hints: The destination is not the case you pass.
Use right and window together.
Choose Case 4.

stages.title: Identify the curious object
stages.setup: In Case 4, the Object keeper sees a folded wing. The Map keeper's inventory says the object has a round dial. The Label keeper's note says it is made of paper.
cards: Clockwork Kite | folded wing, round dial, paper
Sun Compass | no wing, round dial, paper
Silver Moth | folded wing, no dial, metal
stages.prompt: Which invented object fits all three records?
stages.why: Only Clockwork Kite has a wing, dial and paper material.
hints: Each role has one necessary fact.
Reject objects that fail even one fact.
Clockwork Kite is the only full match.

stages.title: Restore the object label
stages.setup: The Clockwork Kite record says it is a pretend paper instrument for tracing an imaginary breeze. Do not choose a label about real history or a powered machine.
cards: Label A | A royal metal clock from 1800
Label B | A pretend paper breeze-tracing kite
Label C | A motorised weather balloon
stages.prompt: Which label tells the object's true fictional story?
stages.why: Label B matches the invented paper object's stated purpose.
hints: Keep the object fictional.
Look for paper and breeze.
Label B says both.

stages.title: Complete the exhibition sheet
stages.setup: The opening sheet needs the gallery, case, object and label already found. A wrong field means visitors would see the wrong exhibit.
cards: Sheet A | Amber / Case 4 / Clockwork Kite / Label B
Sheet B | Blue / Case 4 / Clockwork Kite / Label B
Sheet C | Amber / Case 7 / Silver Moth / Label A
stages.prompt: Which opening sheet uses the complete evidence trail?
stages.why: Sheet A agrees with each prior result.
hints: Read your four earlier results in order.
Check gallery and case first.
All fields on Sheet A match.
stages.skip: Use Sheet A and read the ending.

games.title: The Missing Final Chapter
games.opening: A fictional storybook has lost its final page. Each reading group holds a different clue. Put the pages back in order before choosing the ending that fits.
games.ending: The librarian places the recovered page into the book. The story can now be read from beginning to end.

stages.title: Follow the index symbol
stages.setup: The missing book's index slip has a BLUE moon above a small key. Shelf M has blue moon and key; Shelf P has blue star and key; Shelf T has red moon and key.
stages.prompt: Which shelf holds this story?
stages.why: Shelf M matches both the blue moon and key.
hints: Match both symbol and colour word.
A star is not a moon.
Shelf M has the exact pair.

stages.title: Find the page bundle
stages.setup: The Shelf M ledger says the book has SEVEN paper leaves and a violet ribbon. Bundle M7 has seven leaves and violet ribbon; M4 has four leaves; P7 has seven leaves but is on another shelf.
stages.prompt: Which bundle should the group open?
stages.why: M7 matches shelf, leaf count and ribbon.
hints: Keep the shelf letter from the index.
Count leaves and check ribbon.
M7 matches every detail.

stages.title: Put the middle events in order
stages.setup: The M7 pages say the Lantern is lit before anyone crosses the Bridge. The Garden gate opens only after the crossing. The three role readers each hold one of those facts.
stages.prompt: What is the only possible story order?
stages.why: Lantern must precede Bridge, and Garden follows Bridge.
hints: Find the event that must happen first.
The Garden cannot precede the Bridge.
The order is L-B-G.

stages.title: Read the final-page index
stages.setup: The librarian's index maps story orders to page pockets: L-G-B goes to Pocket 2; L-B-G goes to Pocket 9; B-L-G goes to Pocket 5.
stages.prompt: Where is the missing page?
stages.why: The correct earlier order L-B-G maps to Pocket 9.
hints: Use your sequence exactly.
Do not swap Bridge and Garden.
Look in Pocket 9.

stages.title: Choose a fitting ending
stages.setup: The recovered Page 9 says the group used the lantern to guide friends safely across, then shared a map of the garden. The ending must follow that action without adding a new unexplained quest.
cards: Ending A | They hid the lantern and forgot the garden.
Ending B | They shared the garden map and went home together.
Ending C | A rocket appeared and took everyone to the Moon.
stages.prompt: Which ending completes this story?
stages.why: Ending B follows the recovered page's sharing and group journey.
hints: The ending should grow from Page 9.
Avoid new events without clues.
Ending B continues the shared map story.
stages.skip: Use Ending B and read the librarian's reply.

games.title: The Lost Forecast Bulletin
games.opening: The paper observatory lost its fictional bulletin. Three teams each hold one type of symbol card. Compare the printed rules and rebuild the notice.
games.ending: The station posts its pretend bulletin. Every symbol can be checked against the paper key your team used.

stages.title: Choose the observation day
stages.setup: The station mark is a BLUE triangle above TWO short lines. Day 3 has blue triangle + two lines; Day 1 has blue triangle + one line; Day 5 has red triangle + two lines.
stages.prompt: Which day belongs to this station mark?
stages.why: Day 3 matches both the colour word and two lines.
hints: Check the triangle and line count.
Two lines alone do not decide the day.
Day 3 has both marks.

stages.title: Find the map grid
stages.setup: The date chart gives Day 1 -> A1, Day 3 -> B2, Day 5 -> C3. The answer is a map grid, not a weather prediction.
stages.prompt: Which grid should the teams inspect?
stages.why: Day 3 maps to B2.
hints: Bring the exact day from checkpoint 1.
Read the middle date-chart row.
Inspect B2.

stages.title: Combine the symbol teams
stages.setup: At B2, Cloud readers report TWO cloud circles. Wind readers report an arrow pointing RIGHT. Rain readers report ONE drop. All three printed facts are needed.
cards: Set A | 2 clouds, right arrow, 1 drop
Set B | 2 clouds, left arrow, 1 drop
Set C | 1 cloud, right arrow, 2 drops
stages.prompt: Which symbol set matches B2?
stages.why: Set A alone has two clouds, right arrow and one drop.
hints: Ask all three teams to speak.
Check arrow direction after counting symbols.
Set A is the full match.

stages.title: Put the bulletin strips in order
stages.setup: For Set A, the station rule says wind is announced first, cloud second and rain last. These are pretend symbol categories, not a real forecast.
stages.prompt: What is the correct bulletin order?
stages.why: The printed Set A rule places W before C before R.
hints: Find the first and last categories.
W comes first, R last.
C belongs between W and R.

stages.title: Post the checked bulletin
stages.setup: The station posts only a sheet with the day, map grid, complete symbol set and strip order your teams verified.
cards: Sheet A | Day 3 / B2 / Set A / W-C-R
Sheet B | Day 3 / C3 / Set A / W-C-R
Sheet C | Day 5 / B2 / Set B / C-W-R
stages.prompt: Which sheet is supported by the paper observations?
stages.why: Sheet A is the only sheet matching all previous outputs.
hints: Check the day before the symbols.
One wrong field invalidates a bulletin.
All four fields match Sheet A.
stages.skip: Use Sheet A and read the station ending.

games.title: The Great Blueprint Relay
games.opening: The workshop's paper-only pretend machine has lost its display blueprint. Teams need to choose the correct sheet, combine three safety notes and explain the order on paper. Nothing is built or powered.
games.ending: The inventor pins up the checked paper blueprint. Visitors can follow the pretend idea without handling a real tool.

stages.title: Find the design code
stages.setup: The inventory slip calls for a TRIANGLE gear mark and TWO square tabs. P7 has triangle gear + two tabs; P4 has triangle gear + one tab; Q7 has circle gear + two tabs.
stages.prompt: Which paper design code matches?
stages.why: P7 matches both printed marks.
hints: Use both the gear shape and tab count.
Two tabs without the right gear are not enough.
P7 matches everything.

stages.title: Pick the blueprint sheet
stages.setup: The P7 register calls for a long base with two round windows. Frame B has both; Frame A has one window; Frame C has two windows but a short base.
cards: Frame A | long base, one window
Frame B | long base, two windows
Frame C | short base, two windows
stages.prompt: Which drawing belongs to P7?
stages.why: Frame B alone matches the long base and two windows.
hints: Keep the P7 register in view.
Check both base length and window count.
Choose Frame B.

stages.title: Share the three constraint cards
stages.setup: For Frame B, the Designer wants a BLUE paper gear. The Checker needs a SHORT paper belt. The Explainer needs a RED display flag. Compare all three role cards aloud.
cards: Kit 1 | blue gear, long belt, red flag
Kit 2 | blue gear, short belt, red flag
Kit 3 | yellow gear, short belt, red flag
stages.prompt: Which paper kit fits every role?
stages.why: Kit 2 has the blue gear, short belt and red flag.
hints: Each role contributes one condition.
A single wrong part rejects the kit.
Kit 2 satisfies all three.

stages.title: Order the display cards
stages.setup: The Kit 2 display rule says: FOLD the paper base first, ALIGN the printed gear symbol next, and TURN the paper instruction card last. These are story cards, not steps for a real mechanism.
stages.prompt: Which written order belongs on the blueprint?
stages.why: The printed order is fold, align, turn.
hints: Start with the base.
Turn the instruction card last.
Align belongs in the middle.

stages.title: Complete the display blueprint
stages.setup: The final sheet must list the correct design code, frame, kit and written card order. Keep this a paper display; no child has to make or operate a device.
cards: Board A | P7 / Frame B / Kit 2 / F-A-T
Board B | P7 / Frame C / Kit 2 / F-A-T
Board C | Q7 / Frame B / Kit 1 / A-F-T
stages.prompt: Which board can the group explain with its evidence?
stages.why: Board A carries all four earned results in order.
hints: Read the earlier results aloud.
Check every field, not only the title.
Board A agrees with all four checkpoints.
stages.skip: Use Board A and read the workshop ending.
